chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to assign the liability for the offense of the mentally impaired person to his ʿāqilah, whether accidental or intentional.

key_terms.جِنَايَةَ الْمَعْتُوهِ: the offense committed by a mentally impaired person
key_terms.عَاقِلَتِهِ: his agnatic family group responsible for blood-money liability

ai.seo_question: Who bears liability for the offense of a mentally impaired person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling attributed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning the financial liability of a mentally impaired person. It places the burden of his offense upon his ʿāqilah, indicating a rule within the law of injury and compensation.
